title: Finding setups before the move - not just stocks that have already run
author: One-Cellist-8159
selftext:
One thing that frustrates me about trading tools: they’re great at showing you what already moved. Finding something worth researching *before* the obvious breakout or breakdown is harder.

I’ve been thinking about this more with the possibility of lower S&P 500 returns over the next decade. Nobody knows how that plays out, but even a sluggish index can hide very different opportunities underneath.

That’s part of why I built **EdgeCipher’s Market Intelligence module**. It’s a visual way to explore where potential accumulation or distribution pressure is developing across the market and identify individual stocks worth a closer look - on both the bullish and bearish sides.

Some names it’s currently putting on my research list:

* **Bearish setups to investigate:** DIS, SNDK
* **Bullish setups to investigate:** BA, PEG, FDX, PKG, UNH, WELL, AMAT, QCOM

These aren’t automatic buy or short calls. They’re starting points for research, confirmation, and risk planning. A developing setup can fail, and inferred accumulation/distribution isn’t proof of what institutions are doing.

The goal is simple: **spend less time searching and more time evaluating a manageable list of potential setups.**

On this page, it will be very easy to look at relative performance of different sectors [https://edgecipher.ai/market-stream](https://edgecipher.ai/market-stream)

Full disclosure: I’m the builder. If this sounds useful, you can check it out at [**EdgeCipher.ai**](http://edgecipher.ai/) . I’d genuinely appreciate feedback, especially from part-time swing traders.

**What’s harder for you: finding a setup early, or deciding whether it’s worth taking?**
